decisions.reason: CH35 establishes the second line's oversight role and framework; CH34 details the QC procedures that operationalize this oversight within the first and second lines.
Both CPs discuss money laundering methods (mules vs. mixers) but share only a broad topic; there is no direct framework application or illustration relationship.
Both discuss advanced analytical techniques in AFC but cover different specific models (Generative AI vs. Network Analysis) without a direct structural dependency or comparison.
GDPR definition and TJN indices are distinct regulatory and advocacy frameworks; they share a broad privacy/secrecy domain but lack a direct grounding or contrast relationship.
CH21_S04_001 defines the TJN indices and their secrecy/tax haven rankings; CH21_S04_002 directly applies these indices in customer risk assessment procedures.
PEP classification defines types but does not provide a framework directly applied or expanded by PEP screening outsourcing procedures; they are merely related PEP topics.
CH41 outlines the SAR filing step in the investigation process; CH49 expands and operationalizes this step by detailing the specific required fields and information for the SAR form.
General banking vulnerability factors and wire transfer red flags are related risk topics but lack a direct structural dependency; wire transfer risks do not directly apply the general factor list.
Operational effectiveness of controls and AI piloting/expectation setting are distinct operational topics; there is no direct framework application or summary relationship.

Trust-based cybercrime methods and network analysis are related to illicit activities but represent different concepts (crime method vs. detection technique) without a direct grounding or illustration link.
